data.name: Police Quest: SWAT
data.detailed_description:
Two figures appear in the scope of your rifle; an enraged attacker and his trembling hostage. In one single moment, all your training comes down to these two faces in the crosshairs, and your finger on the trigger. The shot is yours.

It's all in a day's work for members of the most elite force in crime fighting history: SWAT, the Special Weapons And Tactics team. Now you can experience this relentless adrenaline-pumping action firsthand as you begin your training as a SWAT officer. After instruction in actual SWAT tactics and target training sessions your skills will be called into action in multiple scenarios and career-advancing missions.

Innocent lives rely on your split-second decision making and your team's courage in the face of incredible danger.

reviews.review:
Police Quest: SWAT represents a significant turning point not only for Sierra's long-running Police Quest series but also for tactical games as a whole. Developed and published by Sierra On-Line, the title abandons the detective-focused gameplay of earlier entries in favor of a realistic portrayal of life within a Special Weapons and Tactics unit. Rather than throwing players into constant shootouts, the game places a strong emphasis on training, discipline, and understanding police procedures. Even decades after its original release, it remains an intriguing piece of gaming history that showcases Sierra's willingness to experiment with emerging CD-ROM technology and interactive storytelling.

The experience begins with players joining the ranks as a prospective SWAT officer, learning the fundamentals of the profession through extensive instruction and practical exercises. The game's descriptions emphasize authenticity, and that commitment is evident throughout the campaign. Missions are framed around the responsibilities of tactical law enforcement, requiring players to think carefully about their actions instead of charging into dangerous situations. Training modules cover everything from proper weapon handling to coordinated room entry techniques, creating an experience that feels more like an interactive academy than a traditional action game. This slower pace may not appeal to everyone, but it gives the title a unique identity that separates it from many police-themed games released before and after it.

One of the game's most memorable elements is its use of full-motion video. Police Quest: SWAT was released during a period when developers embraced live actors and cinematic presentation, and Sierra leaned heavily into that trend. Briefings, instructional segments, and story moments are delivered through FMV sequences that add personality and authenticity to the experience. While modern audiences may view the visuals as dated, they possess a nostalgic charm that complements the game's grounded tone. The performances vary in quality, but the cast successfully conveys the seriousness of the situations being portrayed, helping immerse players in the role of an officer tasked with protecting civilians under high-pressure circumstances.

Gameplay itself is a mixture of point-and-click mechanics, tactical decision-making, and procedural problem solving. The title expects players to follow instructions carefully, and deviating from established procedures can quickly result in mission failure. At times, this strict design philosophy can become frustrating, particularly when objectives require very specific actions or timing. However, that rigidity is also central to the game's appeal. Police Quest: SWAT consistently reinforces the idea that elite law enforcement work depends on preparation, communication, and precision. In many ways, it laid the groundwork for later tactical experiences that would further refine these concepts in the years to come.

The campaign's mission structure steadily increases in intensity, culminating in larger operations involving hostage scenarios and terrorist threats. Despite the escalating stakes, the game never abandons its commitment to realism. Success is measured not by the number of enemies eliminated but by completing objectives responsibly and minimizing unnecessary casualties. This philosophy remains refreshing, especially when compared to many action titles that prioritize spectacle above all else. The game's educational undertones may occasionally overshadow its entertainment value, but they also make it one of the more distinctive entries in Sierra's extensive catalog.

Looking back, Police Quest: SWAT is perhaps most important for its legacy. It served as the foundation for future SWAT titles that would become highly regarded among fans of tactical shooters. Although its interface and mechanics undeniably show their age, its influence is easy to recognize. Players interested in the evolution of the genre will find plenty to appreciate in its design choices, while those with a fondness for classic PC gaming will likely enjoy its nostalgic presentation and ambitious scope.

Police Quest: SWAT is not an easy recommendation for every modern player. Its deliberate pacing, dated controls, and reliance on strict procedural gameplay can create barriers for newcomers. Nevertheless, its dedication to authenticity and its role in shaping tactical police simulations make it a worthwhile experience for anyone interested in gaming history. It stands as an ambitious experiment from Sierra On-Line, demonstrating that realism and methodical gameplay could coexist in an era dominated by arcade-inspired action.

Rating: 5/10
